title: Should I sell my Penang condo at a loss to free up a 90% loan?
excerpt: A 38-year-old already sold a Cyberjaya unit at a loss and now wants to sell a Penang condo below cost to buy something better. Sean agrees with cutting losses, and explains room rental and getting past two loans.

qa.asker: R, a viewer who wrote in by email
qa.context: R is 38 and lives in Perak. He and his wife bought two investment properties on hearsay. He sold the Cyberjaya unit after six years for RM210,000, about RM40,000 less than he paid. He bought a Penang condo five years ago for RM610,000; agents now value it at about RM560,000, and it is let for RM1,800. He wants to sell it to free up his 90% loan for a property with cashback and cash flow, possibly rented out room by room.
qa.question: Is cutting his losses wise, is renting room by room better than a normal tenancy, and how can someone with both 90% loans used buy a third property?
qa.quote: I'm absolutely agreeable to cutting losses just to open up slots to get more.
qa.answer: Yes, sell, if the money and loan it frees can go into a clearly better property. A monthly drain hurts more than a one-off loss. Renting by the room works near offices and colleges but not in family areas. Beyond two 90% loans you need partners, refinancing outside CCRIS, or bulk-purchase discounts.

reasons.title: Opportunity cost outweighs a one-off loss
reasons.body: Sean sold his own semi-detached house at a loss because its large monthly instalments held him back more than the loss did. Cash flow matters more than paper losses.

reasons.title: Rent shows demand before prices do
reasons.body: Cyberjaya has jobs, universities, malls and good roads, yet high-rise rents and prices kept falling while its landed homes did well. Checking rents before buying would have shown the weak demand.

reasons.title: Room rental depends on the tenants nearby
reasons.body: Splitting a unit into rooms, and turning unused common areas into more rooms or a pantry, can raise income near offices and colleges. Large operators should clear it with the management body first, since it affects security and facilities.

reasons.title: Past the second loan takes more work
reasons.body: Options include buying with family or friends under a proper agreement, refinancing existing loans into a facility outside CCRIS at a somewhat higher rate, as Sean has done, or bulk purchases with larger discounts.

actions: Find out exactly what is owed on the Penang condo before selling.
Check the rents of any next property before committing to it.
Assess who rents near a unit before splitting it into rooms.
Check the advice of anyone recommending a property, especially if they earn commission on it.
Do your own due diligence even when a trusted person recommends a project.
qa.caveat: The old flipping stories no longer work, partly because of property gains tax on early sales. Selling only helps if the next deal is genuinely better, so line it up before cutting the loss.

sourceNote: Summarised from Sean's full English captions for Asking Sean #192. The quoted line is verbatim; everything else is paraphrased. Figures are as the viewer stated them in November 2022. Sean shares the contact of a mortgage specialist who helped him refinance, and mentions bulk-purchase companies; loan and tax rules change, so check current ones.
